_note: Grandstand guide content sourced from Gbrain grandstand-guides/* (source-cited, verified 2026-06-15). Corner mappings and covered flags taken from those guides. viewRating is Gbrain's 1-10 Overall scaled to 1-5. Keyed by DB circuit name. Consumed by scripts/seed-grandstands.ts.

Silverstone Circuit.name: Club Corner (B/C)
Silverstone Circuit.bestFor: Best overall — final-corner overtaking, pit lane, podium & start/finish
pros: Covered (a big plus in British weather)
Overtaking plus podium in one seat
cons: Premium pricing
Sells out early
Silverstone Circuit.description: The most complete seat at Silverstone — final-corner passing with the pit lane, podium and start/finish all in view, and it's roofed.

Silverstone Circuit.name: Landostand (Stowe)
Silverstone Circuit.bestFor: Best action — heavy braking into Stowe
pros: New 16,000-seat wrap-around stand
Big braking and overtaking
cons: Sold out for 2026
Uncovered
Silverstone Circuit.description: The old Stowe stands were demolished and replaced by a single 16,000-seat wrap-around grandstand overlooking the Stowe braking zone.

Silverstone Circuit.name: Becketts
pros: The single most spectacular sequence in F1
Good value
cons: Away from overtaking spots
Silverstone Circuit.description: Overlooks the Maggotts–Becketts–Chapel complex, the most spectacular high-speed sequence on the calendar.

Silverstone Circuit.name: Abbey (A/B)
Silverstone Circuit.bestFor: Best for first-timers — Turn 1 & lap starts
pros: First-corner action
Good big-screen coverage
cons: Uncovered
Silverstone Circuit.description: Overlooks the opening Abbey corner where lap-1 action unfolds.

Silverstone Circuit.name: Copse (A/B/C)
pros: Iconic fast corner
Covered options available
cons: Away from the main braking zones
Silverstone Circuit.description: Overlooks the legendary Copse corner taken at over 180mph; A/B/C all have covered options.

Circuit de Monaco.name: Grandstand A (Sainte-Dévote / Pit straight)
Circuit de Monaco.bestFor: Best action — lap-1 launches & main overtaking point
pros: The circuit's main overtaking/incident point
Start-line launches
cons: Premium price
Uncovered
Circuit de Monaco.description: Overlooks the Sainte-Dévote first corner and pit straight — the best lap-1 launch and overtaking view in Monaco.

Circuit de Monaco.name: Grandstand K (Tabac / Port Hercule)
pros: The widest sweep of track from any stand
Iconic harbour backdrop
cons: Premium price
Circuit de Monaco.description: Runs along the harbour front from Sainte-Dévote toward Tabac, giving the widest sweep of track of any Monaco stand.

Circuit de Monaco.name: Grandstand T (Pool exit / Rascasse)
pros: Best pit-lane/garage/pit-stop view in Monaco
Top rows (X/Y/Z/ZA) are covered
cons: Away from the fastest sections
Circuit de Monaco.description: Overlooks the Pool exit down to Rascasse and the pit lane; two screens sit on the barriers opposite and the top rows are the only properly roofed mainstream seats at Monaco.

Circuit de Monaco.name: Grandstand L (Nouvelle Chicane)
pros: The best overtaking spot on the circuit
Cars braking hard from the tunnel
cons: Very expensive
Sells out early
Circuit de Monaco.description: Overlooks the Nouvelle Chicane at the tunnel exit — the only real passing place on the Monaco street circuit.

Circuit de Monaco.name: Grandstand B (Casino Square)
Circuit de Monaco.bestFor: Photography & comfort — the classic Casino backdrop
pros: Casino de Monte-Carlo and Hotel de Paris in frame
Classic Monaco backdrop
cons: No big screen
Cars pass quickly
Circuit de Monaco.description: Sits opposite the Casino de Monte-Carlo with the Hotel de Paris in frame — the most scenic stand on the circuit.

Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps.name: Gold 3 (Eau Rouge / Raidillon)
Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps.bestFor: Best overall — the most famous corner in F1
pros: Overlooks the legendary uphill esses
High on the hill and roofed
cons: Premium price
Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps.description: Overlooks the Eau Rouge–Raidillon complex; it sits high on the hill and is roofed after the recent works.

Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps.name: Gold 8 (La Source / Turn 1)
pros: The best first-corner view at Spa
Frequent lap-1 overtakes
cons: Slow-speed corner
Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps.description: Overlooks the La Source hairpin right after the start — the best first-corner view at Spa.

Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps.name: Gold 1 (Pit straight)
pros: Start/finish line, pit lane and pit stops
Covered
cons: Away from the fastest corners
Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps.description: Opposite the pits on the start/finish straight with a view of the pit stops and podium; it is covered.

Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps.name: Combes (1-4)
Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps.bestFor: Best value — where the real overtaking happens
pros: The cheapest proper seat
Real overtaking into Les Combes
cons: Uncovered
Further from the pit complex
Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps.description: The cheapest proper seat at Spa, overlooking Les Combes at the end of the Kemmel Straight where much of the overtaking happens.

Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps.name: Silver 3 (Pouhon)
pros: The daunting Pouhon double-left
Covered from 2026
cons: No big screen
Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps.description: Overlooks the fast Pouhon double-left; covered from 2026 onward.

Autodromo Nazionale Monza.name: Grandstand 26 (Laterale Destra)
pros: The grid, full pit lane and stops, podium and finish line
The most complete single view at Monza
cons: Away from the braking zones
Autodromo Nazionale Monza.description: Opposite the pits on the start/finish straight — the grid, the full pit lane and stops, the podium and the finish line, the most complete single view at Monza.

Autodromo Nazionale Monza.name: Grandstand 8 (Prima Variante)
Autodromo Nazionale Monza.bestFor: Best action — heavy braking & lap-1 chaos
pros: Biggest braking zone on the calendar
Best braking/photo and lap-1 chaos
cons: Uncovered
Autodromo Nazionale Monza.description: Outside the first chicane at the end of the main straight — the biggest braking zone on the calendar and lap-1 chaos.

Autodromo Nazionale Monza.name: Grandstand 6 (Alta Velocità)
pros: Inside line into Turn 1
Frequent overtakes
cons: Uncovered
Autodromo Nazionale Monza.description: On the inside of the Prima Variante with a view of the cars turning in and the main straight.

Autodromo Nazionale Monza.name: Grandstands 18-20 (Uscita Ascari)
Autodromo Nazionale Monza.bestFor: Best value — real overtaking on the back straight
pros: Cheap with real overtaking
Grandstand 18 is covered
cons: Further from the pit complex
Autodromo Nazionale Monza.description: Cheap seats at the exit of Ascari onto the back straight where real overtaking happens; Grandstand 18 is covered.

Autodromo Nazionale Monza.name: Grandstand 22 (Parabolica)
pros: Classic final corner onto the main straight
Full roof
cons: Away from first-corner action
Autodromo Nazionale Monza.description: Overlooks the long Parabolica leading onto the start/finish straight and has a full roof.

Circuit of The Americas.name: Turn 15 Grandstand
Circuit of The Americas.bestFor: Best overall — multi-corner with the sun behind you
pros: Multi-corner view plus passing
Sun behind you and the best amenities
cons: Away from Turn 1
Circuit of The Americas.description: Overlooks the Turn 12-15 complex with passing action, the sun behind you and the best amenities on site.

Circuit of The Americas.name: Turn 12 Grandstand
Circuit of The Americas.bestFor: Best value/action — best overtaking with an 11-corner panorama
pros: Best overtaking spot
An 11-corner panorama for the price
cons: Uncovered
Circuit of The Americas.description: The heavy braking zone at the end of the back straight — the best overtaking with an 11-corner panorama for the price.

Circuit of The Americas.name: Turn 1 Grandstand
Circuit of The Americas.bestFor: Best for first-timers — the uphill Turn 1
pros: Dramatic uphill first corner
Sees over the fence
cons: Steep walk up
Uncovered
Circuit of The Americas.description: The steep uphill run to Turn 1 funnels the field into a spectacular braking zone, and the stand sees over the fence.

Circuit of The Americas.name: Turn 19 Grandstand
Circuit of The Americas.bestFor: Final corner with a covered option
pros: Upper rows (15-21) are covered
Near the start/finish
cons: Lower rows uncovered
Circuit of The Americas.description: Overlooks the final corner onto the start/finish straight; the upper rows (15-21) are one of only two roofed options at COTA.

Suzuka International Racing Course.name: Grandstand Q2 (Casio Triangle)
Suzuka International Racing Course.bestFor: Best overall — the final chicane, sees 130R
pros: Overtaking at the Casio Triangle chicane
High stand that also sees 130R
cons: Premium price
Suzuka International Racing Course.description: A high stand over the Casio Triangle chicane and final corner that also sees 130R and the pit entry — Suzuka's best overtaking view.

Suzuka International Racing Course.name: Grandstand D (The Esses)
Suzuka International Racing Course.bestFor: Best value — car balance through the S-curves
pros: The best display of car and driver on the limit on the calendar
Great value
cons: No big screen (lower blocks)
Suzuka International Racing Course.description: Overlooks the flowing S-curves (the Esses) where the best drivers make the difference — the best display of car/driver on the limit on the calendar.

Suzuka International Racing Course.name: Grandstand B (First Curve)
Suzuka International Racing Course.bestFor: Best action — lap-1 incidents at Turn 1/2
pros: Best lap-1 incident seat
Big screen (infield)
cons: Action passes quickly
Suzuka International Racing Course.description: Overlooks the First Curve (Turns 1/2) with an infield big screen — the best lap-1 incident seat.

Suzuka International Racing Course.name: Grandstand V2 (Main straight)
pros: Start/finish and pit view
Upper rows partly covered
cons: Away from the fast corners
Suzuka International Racing Course.description: Overlooks the main straight, start/finish and pit lane; the upper rows are partly covered, among the only roofed seating at Suzuka.

Bahrain International Circuit.name: Turn 1 Grandstand
Bahrain International Circuit.bestFor: Best overall & best action — overtaking purists who want the marquee braking-zone pass
viewsOf: Turn 1-2-3-4 sequence from high rows in sections P, R, S
pros: Best overtaking at the track
Multi-corner view down to Turn 4 from high rows
Better value than Main
cons: Big screens are distant — bring binoculars
Grid-end blocks push the Turn 1 apex away
Bahrain International Circuit.description: Outside the circuit at the end of the main straight, wrapping Turn 1: you get the heavy DRS braking zone and the best overtaking move of the lap, plus a view back up the main straight and the pit exit.

Bahrain International Circuit.name: Beyon Grandstand (formerly Batelco / Oasis)
Bahrain International Circuit.bestFor: Best value — photographers and fans who want to see the most of the lap
viewsOf: Third DRS zone and the Turn 11 braking zone
Distant glimpses of Turns 3-4 and Turns 13-14
pros: Unmatched track coverage at mid price
Open and panoramic — the photographer's pick
Fewest reported fence obstructions
cons: Only one big screen, and it is distant
Loses the cars after Turn 10; no finish-line view
Bahrain International Circuit.description: Inside the circuit behind the pit building on the inner straight through the Turn 9-10-11 area, it offers the most panoramic view at Bahrain — a sweeping vista of roughly Turns 6 to 12 including the third DRS zone.

Bahrain International Circuit.name: Main Grandstand
Bahrain International Circuit.bestFor: Best for first-timers — grid walk, start, pit stops and podium; also the family pick
viewsOf: Pit lane and pit stops over the wall
Main straight / DRS run toward Turn 1
pros: Ceremony: grid walk, start, podium
Three large screens directly opposite
Best facilities and easiest exits, next to the Fan Zone
cons: Weakest stand for actual racing
The priciest tickets at the circuit
Bahrain International Circuit.description: Along the inside of the main straight opposite the pit lane and start/finish line, it delivers the start, pit stops, finish and podium, but little mid-lap action once the cars have gone.

Bahrain International Circuit.name: University Grandstand (1, 2, 3)
Bahrain International Circuit.bestFor: Budget-conscious fans wanting comprehensive viewing — University 2, sections C or D, high rows
viewsOf: Turn 1 overtaking from an outside angle
Infield around Turns 9-10 (from the right sub-section)
Acceleration out of Turn 1 toward Turn 4 / DRS Zone 2
pros: Budget price with TV screens directly opposite University 2
Dual Turn 1 and infield view from University 2
cons: University 1 can partially block University 2 at apex level
10-15 minute walk across open ground to the main food vendors
Bahrain International Circuit.description: On the rising ground outside the circuit by the Turns 2-3 area, it gives Turn 1 overtaking from a different angle plus, from the right sub-section, the infield around Turns 9-10.

Bahrain International Circuit.name: Victory Grandstand 2
Bahrain International Circuit.bestFor: Strict budget with a real final-corner view
pros: Cheapest tickets at the circuit
Sees the final corner, where late-lap moves happen
Good for low-speed final-corner car photos
cons: Furthest from the main precinct, with thinner facilities
Quiet atmosphere, a long way from the Fan Zone
Bahrain International Circuit.description: Outside the circuit toward the final corners at the end of the back straight, Victory 2 sees the final corner(s) and a slice of start/finish, with overtaking possible at the apex.

Bahrain International Circuit.name: Victory Grandstand 1
Bahrain International Circuit.bestFor: Avoid — the page's designated worst pick at this circuit
pros: Cheapest tickets at the circuit
cons: The weakest sightline at the track
Isolated and quiet, far from the Fan Zone
Bahrain International Circuit.description: The guide's explicit 'avoid' pick: Victory 1's view is limited to essentially a distant Turn 11, with little action, isolation from the main precinct and a quiet atmosphere.

Baku City Circuit.name: Absheron (Main) Grandstand — Section E
Baku City Circuit.bestFor: Best overall (and joint best action) — overtaking seekers who also want the start, pit stops and podium
pros: Banks start, pits, podium and the Turn 1 braking lunge
Big screen clearly visible; best amenities and fan zone behind
High rows see over pit equipment and across to Turn 1
cons: Priciest stand on the circuit
Sections D/E are open — no cover, unlike Sections A-C
Baku City Circuit.description: High rows of Section E sit at the Turn 1 end of the main grandstand, adding the lap's biggest braking-and-overtaking zone to the start, pit-lane action and podium in front of you.

Baku City Circuit.name: Absheron (Main) Grandstand — Sections A-C
Baku City Circuit.bestFor: Best for first-timers — families and comfort seekers wanting grid, podium and the circuit's only roofed seats
pros: Sections A-C are partially covered — the only roofed seats on the circuit
Grid, pit stops and podium ceremony directly in front
Screens, food, toilets and the Purple Zone fan zone immediately behind
cons: Priciest stand; Section B sells out first
Straights-and-pits focus means less cornering action than Section E
Baku City Circuit.description: The central sections of the main grandstand are the ceremony end — grid, pit stops and podium — and the only partially covered seating at Baku, making them the comfort play for a 15:00 start.

Baku City Circuit.name: Azneft Grandstand
Baku City Circuit.bestFor: Overtaking and incident seekers, and photographers who can't afford Absheron Section E
pros: Sits at a real overtaking corner — the lap's second genuine passing point
Strong photography: cars yawing under braking in waterfront light
Higher rows see entry, apex and exit
cons: No cover
Afternoon sun exposure
Baku City Circuit.description: Beside Azneft Square on the waterfront, this stand looks onto the 90-degree Turn 16 braking and exit — heavy braking, lock-ups and lunges at the lap's second-best overtaking corner.

Baku City Circuit.name: Filarmoniya Grandstand
Baku City Circuit.bestFor: Joint best for action — close-up braking drama and photography at Turn 16
pros: Closest look at cars shedding speed — lock-ups, late braking, divebombs
Best braking close-up after Absheron Section E
Higher rows give the full braking arc
cons: No cover
Reported sold out for 2026 via the promoter
Baku City Circuit.description: Sitting inside Turn 16 at the heavy braking point, Filarmoniya gives the circuit's closest view of cars shedding speed into the lap's second overtaking corner.

Baku City Circuit.name: Khazar Grandstand
Baku City Circuit.bestFor: Best value — budget buyers, families and first-timers who want a screen plus raw speed
viewsOf: A second straight section on some setups
pros: Cheapest credible grandstand at Baku — the clear value pick
Simple, fast, unobstructed straight-on view of top speed
Big screen and close to the fan zones
cons: No braking zone — you watch cars pass rather than fight
No cover
Baku City Circuit.description: An infield stand on the main straight where cars flash past at 340+ km/h in DRS trains and slipstream battles — the cheapest credible seat with a screen at the circuit.

Baku City Circuit.name: Bulvar Grandstand
Baku City Circuit.bestFor: Atmosphere plus a bit of action on a budget-to-mid ticket
pros: Corner-plus-straight combo: you see the run that decides a Turn 1 overtake
Strong atmosphere with fan zones and the boulevard nearby
Good food and toilet proximity, walkable
cons: No cover
Not the prime braking zone
Baku City Circuit.description: On the seafront boulevard at the final corner, Bulvar shows cars braking, rotating and firing onto the main straight at the second DRS activation point.

Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya.name: Main Grandstand (Tribuna Principal)
Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya.bestFor: Best overall — grid, pits, podium and start/finish under a roof
pros: Only ticket with pits, podium, covered roof and sun behind you
Standing start, every pit stop and the podium ceremony
Upper Zones 24-28 add Turn 1 visibility plus the left screen
cons: Hard fixed plastic seats and priciest tier
Screens only readable from the ends; no braking/overtaking corner head-on
Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya.description: On the pit straight opposite the pit lane, this is the only stand that combines start, pit stops, podium and a high covered roof, and its roughly northwest orientation puts the sun behind you for the 15:00 start.

Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya.name: Grandstand G (stadium, Turns 12-13)
Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya.bestFor: Best value and best for first-timers — most track per euro, big crowd energy
pros: Most track-for-money on the circuit; sees almost the entire final sector
Big, loud, family-friendly party atmosphere
Easy to follow the race, cheapest seated option
cons: No shade at all - faces between east and south, afternoon sun on the stand
Two infield screens near Turn 10 that 'feel far'; slow corners, not pure overtaking
Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya.description: The largest stand, curving around Turn 12 toward Turn 13 in the technical stadium loop, it shows almost the whole final sector from the back rows (recommended zones ~10-20, highest rows) for the lowest price.

Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya.name: Grandstand E / F / K (Turn 1 cluster)
Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya.bestFor: Best for action — the no.1 overtaking spot and lap-one carnage
pros: Maximum passes and incidents - the single best overtaking spot on the track
Excellent late-braking and side-by-side photography from high rows
cons: Open/uncovered - full sun for a 15:00 race
You see the entry but lose the back half of the lap; heavy screen reliance
Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya.description: The trio of stands around the Turn 1 (Elf) braking zone - E on the straight into Turn 1, F across Turns 1-3 and K on the braking point - watching cars arrive at 300+ km/h and dive down the inside.

Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya.name: Grandstand H (Turn 14, final corner)
Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya.bestFor: Comfort plus final-corner and restart drama (Zones 1-5, high rows only)
viewsOf: Turn 10 braking zone (Zones 1-5, highest rows only)
pros: Only covered stand that sees the final corners
From the right seats, two corners including an overtaking zone
One screen visible from all seats
cons: Zones 6-11 are blocked by trees and the TV screen
Most expensive stand; southwest-facing so front rows catch afternoon sun
Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya.description: Outside the fast Turn 14 opposite the pit-lane entrance, it is covered and adds the Turn 10 braking-zone overtakes - but only from Zones 1-5 in the highest rows, since Zones 6-11 are blocked by trees and the TV screen.

Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya.name: Grandstand A (Turns 1-3)
Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya.bestFor: Overtaking plus shade in one ticket
pros: Covered AND on the main passing corner - a rare combination
First-corner complex face-on with first-lap S-section drama
cons: Pricier than the open stands
Less documented screen sightline and atmosphere than the stadium stands
Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya.description: On the outside of the Turn 1-2-3 complex, it is one of only three roofed stands and the rare option that puts you on the circuit's main overtaking corner while still giving you shade.

Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya.name: Grandstand T10 (La Caixa, Turn 10)
Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya.bestFor: Value overtaking — second-best passing stand, cheaper than Turn 1
viewsOf: End of the back straight / second DRS zone
pros: Second-best overtaking stand on the circuit
Comes alive in the second half of the race
Cheaper than Turn 1 for similar passing
cons: Uncovered, no shade
Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya.description: Sits directly at the Turn 10 (La Caixa) braking zone, the heaviest braking on the lap and the second genuine passing chance - the pick if you want overtakes without paying Turn 1 prices.

Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya.name: Grandstand N (Turns 8-9, Campsa)
Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya.bestFor: Best for action (with the Turn 1 cluster) — fast Campsa and the run to Turn 10
viewsOf: Back straight / second DRS zone toward Turn 10
pros: Fast, spectacular high-speed commitment through Campsa
Lively - popular with Alonso fan clubs
cons: You see the set-up, not the actual Turn 10 pass
Uncovered, no shade
Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya.description: Outside the fast Turn 9 (Campsa) right-hander that feeds the back straight, watching cars commit through the corner and accelerate into the second DRS zone toward the Turn 10 overtake.

Hungaroring.name: Apex 1 (formerly Silver 3)
Hungaroring.bestFor: Best overall — elevated action view over the final-corner complex
pros: Best all-round action view
Elevation over multiple corners plus the straight
Near the GA banking and fanzone
cons: No shade
Mid-price rather than cheap
Hungaroring.description: Elevated on the natural hill above Turn 14, it takes in Turns 12-13-14, the pit entry and the pit straight — the exit battles here set up the passes at Turn 1, making it the highest-density action view at the circuit.

Hungaroring.name: T1 Grandstand (formerly Gold 4)
Hungaroring.bestFor: Best for action — the circuit's only true overtaking spot
viewsOf: End of the pit straight / DRS zone
pros: The best overtaking spot at the circuit
Sees the start funnel past you
Much better sightlines than the old Gold 3 stand it superseded
cons: No shade, full afternoon exposure
Catch fence hampers the low rows
Hungaroring.description: On the outside of Turn 1 at the end of the straight, this stand overlooks the downhill hard-braking zone where the late lunges, lock-ups, first-lap chaos and safety-car restarts happen.

Hungaroring.name: Hungaroring Grandstand (formerly Super Gold)
Hungaroring.bestFor: Best for first-timers — shade, start, podium, pits and screens
pros: The only covered stand at the circuit
Start, podium, pit activity and four TV screens opposite
Central, shortest walk to facilities
cons: Premium price (~EUR 660 for 3 days)
No on-track overtaking — passing happens at Turn 1, out of view
Hungaroring.description: The rebuilt centrepiece stand on the main straight opposite the pit garages, with a roof over the upper rows and four TV screens spaced along the pit building — the comfort pick for a 15:00 start.

Hungaroring.name: Grand Prix 2 (formerly Silver 4 hill)
Hungaroring.bestFor: Best fallback if Apex 1 is sold out; panoramic final-corner photography
pros: Excellent panoramic view from the hill
Final-corner battles and exit runs
High rows great for sweeping photo pans
cons: No shade, full exposure
Hungaroring.description: Set on the hill behind the final-corner complex, its elevation gives panoramic views over Turns 12-14 and the pit straight, covering the exit runs that set up the DRS move into Turn 1.

Hungaroring.name: Chicane 3 (formerly Super Bronze)
Hungaroring.bestFor: Photographers — the widest multi-corner view in the infield
pros: Panoramic view over Turns 4 to 8
Numbered seats with a large screen in front
Best infield panorama for sweep shots
cons: No shade and far from start/finish
Little overtaking in this sector
Hungaroring.description: The elevated vantage point in Sector 2, giving the widest single-stand multi-corner view in the infield across Turns 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8.

Hungaroring.name: Chicane 1 (formerly Bronze 1)
Hungaroring.bestFor: Best value — ~EUR 330 reserved seat over the technical sector
pros: ~EUR 330 reserved seat — exceptional value
Relaxed and photo-friendly
Good close-up of the technical sweep, screen in front
cons: Long walk to the main action and fanzone
Minimal overtaking
Hungaroring.description: A Sector 2 stand around Turn 5 looking over the fast direction changes of the mid-lap esses — a watch-the-car-dance section rather than a watch-the-fight one, at the cheapest reserved-seat price on the calendar.

Hungaroring.name: Chicane 2 (formerly Bronze 2)
Hungaroring.bestFor: Best value — ~EUR 330 reserved seat, slightly better angle than Chicane 1
pros: Slightly better angle than Chicane 1
Near Gate 3 for the shuttle buses
~EUR 330 reserved seat — exceptional value
cons: Long walk to the main action and fanzone
Minimal overtaking
Hungaroring.description: The Sector 2 stand around Turns 6-7, with the better viewing angle of the two Bronze chicane stands and handy access to the shuttle buses at Gate 3.

Autódromo José Carlos Pace.name: Grandstand M (Turn 1 / Senna S entry, opposite the pits)
Autódromo José Carlos Pace.bestFor: Best overall and best action — Turn 1 dive-bomb, pits opposite, covered numbered seat
pros: Best overtaking view at the circuit
Covered and numbered/reserved seating
In-stand toilets, food and merch
cons: Priciest lettered seat and sells out fast
Autódromo José Carlos Pace.description: Sited opposite the pits at the end of the main straight and outside Turn 1, M looks straight into the braking zone and the dive into the Senna S — the circuit's best overtaking spot, plus pit-lane activity across the track.

Autódromo José Carlos Pace.name: Grandstand A (final corner / start-finish complex)
Autódromo José Carlos Pace.bestFor: Best value and best for first-timers — cheap panoramic amphitheatre view with the best crowd on the circuit
viewsOf: Panoramic infield view of much of the lap
pros: Cheap with a huge panoramic view
Electric atmosphere — flags, airhorns, samba
Natural tree shade in parts, unique among the cheap stands
cons: Uncovered and storm-exposed
Unreserved concrete bleacher that gets very full
Autódromo José Carlos Pace.description: The circuit's largest stand, wrapping the run out of the final corner onto the main straight with an amphitheatre panorama of much of the lap, and the emotional centre of the Brazilian crowd.

Autódromo José Carlos Pace.name: Grandstand D (Senna S)
Autódromo José Carlos Pace.bestFor: Hardcore fans and photographers who want the Senna S
pros: Iconic corner and covered
Superb photography of cars changing direction through the esses
cons: Premium price
Further from the podium and start
Autódromo José Carlos Pace.description: Sits at the Senna S itself — the left-right-left esses that are the technical heart of the lap, where lap-1 incidents, lock-ups and late dives from the Turn 1 zone get completed.

Autódromo José Carlos Pace.name: Grandstand H (Senna S exit / Curva do Sol)
pros: Rated among the best action stands
Covered, with plenty of passing to watch
cons: Premium price
Far from start/finish and the podium
Autódromo José Carlos Pace.description: Between the Senna S and Curva do Sol, looking at the exit of the esses and the climb to the back straight — one of the best places to watch the S section, with overtakes completed out of it.

Autódromo José Carlos Pace.name: Grandstand B (start/finish line, grid and podium)
Autódromo José Carlos Pace.bestFor: Start, pits and podium ceremony under a roof — families and comfort-seekers
viewsOf: Start of the main straight at the start/finish line
pros: Podium, race start and pit drama in one seat
Covered with numbered/reserved seats
Best rain and sun protection at the circuit
cons: Premium price
Limited overtaking to watch live
Autódromo José Carlos Pace.description: One of only two stands with both numbered seats and a roof, B sits at the start of the main straight on the start/finish line with the grid, pit entry, several garages and the podium in view.

Autódromo José Carlos Pace.name: Grandstand R (Turn 3 / Curva do Sol)
Autódromo José Carlos Pace.bestFor: Photographers and action fans who hate catch fencing
viewsOf: Glimpses of pit exit and the Senna S
pros: Elevated with views unobstructed by catch fencing
Covered, overlooking the multi-corner opening sequence
cons: Premium or package-only on some sellers
Further from the podium
Autódromo José Carlos Pace.description: A raised, covered stand outside Turn 3 / Curva do Sol whose selling point is an elevated, fence-free sightline over the opening corners, with position battles and pit-stop rejoins in view.

Autódromo José Carlos Pace.name: Grandstand G (back straight / Descida do Lago braking zone)
Autódromo José Carlos Pace.bestFor: Budget die-hards and speed fans — cheapest seats at the circuit

Top-speed and DRS-zone action with late-braking passes
Loud, raucous, fun atmosphere

Jeddah Corniche Circuit.name: Main Grandstand B (Start/Finish — Turn 1)
Jeddah Corniche Circuit.bestFor: Best overall and best for action — Turn 1 braking zone plus the start and podium

Covered with a big screen, cheaper than Main A
Better podium view than Main A
cons: Grid and pits are more distant than from Main A

Jeddah Corniche Circuit.name: Main Grandstand A (Start/Finish — opposite the pits)

Covered with a big screen
Easiest logistics, shortest walk from the main entrance
cons: Least actual overtaking — cars are flat past you
Priciest of the main stands

Jeddah Corniche Circuit.name: Central Grandstand A (Turns 5-8 technical loop)

Genuine high-speed technical action
Front-facing, among the cleaner photo angles
cons: Few passes
Far from the podium and pits
Jeddah Corniche Circuit.description: A circuit-exterior stand at the fast technical Turns 5-8, where cars run millimetres from the wall — incident-prone precision corners rather than overtaking.

Jeddah Corniche Circuit.name: Central Grandstand C (Turn 8 exit / Turns 17-18 / final DRS zone)

Sees a DRS zone — the setup for the Turn 1 pass
Good front-facing photography angles

Passes complete elsewhere on the lap
Jeddah Corniche Circuit.description: An opening-sector exterior stand sighting the Turn 8 exit, Turns 17-18 and the final DRS run — arguably the most raw speed of the Central set.

Jeddah Corniche Circuit.name: Central Grandstand B (Turns 5-8 / Turns 19-20 dual view)

Big screen at a low price
cons: Uncovered and distant doubled-back view
No overtakes
Jeddah Corniche Circuit.description: A dual-perspective spot that catches cars twice per lap across two separate stretches, though both are fast walled sections rather than wheel-to-wheel racing.

Jeddah Corniche Circuit.name: Central Grandstand D (Coastal — Turns 8-10 / 16-18)

Cheap
cons: No big screen, so you lose the race narrative
Uncovered and distant
Jeddah Corniche Circuit.description: A coastal position with the prettiest backdrop but the weakest racing utility — doubled-back, far from the action and with no big screen.

Las Vegas Strip Circuit.name: T-Mobile Zone at Sphere (Turns 5-9, SG1-SG8 sectors)

Best photography — cars plus Sphere and neon
Best atmosphere, with live concerts

Higher rows risk stage/screen obstruction

Las Vegas Strip Circuit.name: Heineken Silver Main Grandstand — East Harmon Zone (Start/Finish, Pits, Turn 1)
Las Vegas Strip Circuit.bestFor: Best for action — the Turn 1 braking zone (200 to ~65 mph) is the prime overtaking spot, plus pits and start/finish

Most amenities and the biggest fan zone
Most sheltered footprint (permanent Pit Building behind)

Some blocks obstructed by skybox structures
Las Vegas Strip Circuit.description: Faces the pit lane and starting grid from the permanent Pit Building and runs down toward Turn 1, the heaviest braking point on the lap and the number one passing spot.

Las Vegas Strip Circuit.name: Turn 3 Grandstand — East Harmon Zone (Turns 3-4, Koval Straight)
Las Vegas Strip Circuit.bestFor: Value hunters who want to roam — 2026 ticket includes access to West Harmon, Koval and East Harmon zones

Widest roaming access of any single grandstand ticket for 2026
Close to the big East Harmon fan zone

Brief car-exposure window
Las Vegas Strip Circuit.description: Relocated for 2026 to the west side of Turn 3, looking at drivers attacking Turns 3-4 before they launch down the Koval Straightaway.

Las Vegas Strip Circuit.name: Heineken Grandstands — Koval Zone (Turn 4 exit)
Las Vegas Strip Circuit.bestFor: Best value — cheapest 3-day grandstand with complimentary Heineken for 21+
pros: Cheapest 3-day grandstand (from ~$925 incl. fees)
Complimentary Heineken for 21+
Relaxed, newer and less crowded
cons: Least on-track variety
Bench (assigned bleacher) seating and a lower sightline
Las Vegas Strip Circuit.description: Runs along the left-hand straight immediately after the Turn 4 exit, where cars are hard on the power building top speed down the Koval Straight.

Las Vegas Strip Circuit.name: West Harmon Grandstand — West Harmon Zone (Turns 14/17 area, Harmon Straight)
Las Vegas Strip Circuit.bestFor: Budget speed-chasers who will use the new 2026 roaming access to East Harmon and Koval
pros: Cheap (from ~$1,012 incl. fees)
Visceral top-speed sensation
2026 connection to East Harmon and Koval adds value
cons: Minimal racing and overtaking — cars are flat-out here
Historically the weakest standalone view
Las Vegas Strip Circuit.description: Sits inside the track near the final-corner sequence and pit-lane entry, looking down the Harmon Straight at cars going by at near-max speed.

Lusail International Circuit.name: Main Grandstand (Zones A–F, main straight)

Lusail International Circuit.description: Sitting on the main straight directly opposite the pit garages, it is the best-engineered bank on the circuit — a proper grandstand bowl giving the start, the full grid, pit stops and the podium, with Zones C/D central and mid-to-upper rows the sweet spot.

Lusail International Circuit.name: North Grandstand (Grandstand Nord — Turn 1)

Open seating, so you can sit early and pick your row
Strong photography — Turn 1 braking and the grid launch in one frame
cons: No roof
Unreserved — arrive early for the good upper-row Turn 1 seats
Lusail International Circuit.description: Immediately left of the Main Grandstand between the main straight and Turn 1, it is the action-vs-ceremony compromise: you still see the start and the pits, but you also get the braking and passing at Turn 1 that the Main does not.

Lusail International Circuit.name: T16 Grandstand (Turn 16)
Lusail International Circuit.bestFor: Best value — real overtaking and braking action at a value price, plus the top night-photography corner

Arguably the best night light-streak photography spot
The late-race drama corner — DRS set-up moves and the last push to the flag
cons: Uncovered and unreserved
You miss the start, grid and podium
Lusail International Circuit.description: At the final corner before the main straight, it shows the heavy braking as cars decelerate from high speed into Turn 16 and then fire onto the 1km straight — the second-best action corner after Turn 1.

Lusail International Circuit.name: T2 Grandstand (Turn 2)
Lusail International Circuit.bestFor: Corner action at a mid price with a wider view than a single apex

Near the Turn 1 action without main-straight pricing
cons: Uncovered and unreserved
Further from the start and the ceremonies
Lusail International Circuit.description: Added in 2023 on the inside of Turn 2, it gives a decent multi-corner perspective on early-lap jostling, with higher rows catching the Turn 1 to Turn 3 sweep.

Lusail International Circuit.name: Lusail Hill (General Admission — Turn 1)

The loosest, most party-ish crowd on site

No guaranteed view — arrive early (2+ hours before the 19:00 start)
Lusail International Circuit.description: An elevated public area near Turn 1 and the one GA spot that earns its keep because it is raised — most other general admission at Lusail is flat and fence-blocked.

Lusail International Circuit.name: T3 Grandstand (Turn 3)
Lusail International Circuit.bestFor: The page's explicit AVOID — budget fans who specifically want the early esses and don't mind the hike

Quieter, and usually cheaper
cons: Furthest grandstand from the entrance — the longest walk on the circuit
Least overtaking; Turn 3 is a positioning corner, not a passing one
Lusail International Circuit.description: Added in 2023 near Turn 3 with a superb view back to Turn 2, it offers a fine dual-corner angle, but the corners themselves don't generate passes and it is the longest walk on the circuit.

Madring.name: Gold 1 & Gold 2 — Main Straight (Recta Principal)

Everything ceremonial: grid, podium, pit stops
Turn 1 first-lap chaos and braking
cons: Priciest tier on the circuit
Straight-line cars are less photogenic than a corner
Madring.description: The best view on the circuit per official and vendor framing — the only place you see grid, pits and podium together, with a roof over all but the front rows and direct Metro access at the main entry complex.

Madring.name: Silver Plus 11 & 13 — La Monumental Exit / Turn 13

Bullring-amphitheatre atmosphere, loudest and most partisan crowd

Banking exit is fast, so a pass is not guaranteed
Madring.description: The headline spectacle of the Madring: cars at full lean out of the banked Monumental section into a braking/turn-in passing chance at Turn 13, under cover and for well under Gold money.

Madring.name: Silver 4 & 5 — Turns 4 & 5 (fast section + big brake)

Visceral speed differential, higher rows see approach and apex

Less ceremony than the main straight

Madring.name: La Monumental 9, 10 & 12 — Banked Bowl (support stands)

cons: No roof — full sun
Some angles are secondary to Stands 11/13

Madring.name: Bronze/Silver 14, 15 & 16 — Curvas Enlazadas / Valdebebas (Turns 14–17)

Vendor guides flag 15 and 16 for good overall experience
cons: No shade
Away from the ceremony of the main straight

Madring.name: Silver 6, 7 & 8 — Bunker / Technical (Turns 6–11)

Often cheaper than the headline stands
Higher rows catch multiple corners
cons: Sparse overtaking
Lower rows see one apex and a wall
Madring.description: The uphill/downhill 'Bunker' complex with an 8% climb and a sharp drop between Turns 7 and 9 — driver-skill corners with big sightline variety but few passes.

Albert Park Circuit.name: Fangio Grandstand (Main Straight, on the grid / pit area)

Premium pricing

Albert Park Circuit.name: Piastri Grandstand (Main Straight, new for 2026)

Spectacle and value away from the crowds

Long approach view
cons: Lower rows fight the catch fence
Full sun
Circuit Gilles Villeneuve.description: Sits at the exit of the hairpin with the approach visible nearly back to Turn 9; upper rows give unobstructed views and the best photography after Grandstand 34.

Circuit Gilles Villeneuve.name: Platine (Senna S, T1–2)
Circuit Gilles Villeneuve.bestFor: Best first-timer — comfort-seekers who want a guaranteed dry seat plus the start action
viewsOf: The start-finish launch off the line
Cars rejoining from the pit exit
pros: The only roofed grandstand on the circuit — sun and rain protection
Plastic moulded seats with backs rather than bare metal bleacher
Start action plus a big-screen sightline
cons: Priciest non-hospitality option
You watch the back half of the lap on screen
Circuit Gilles Villeneuve.description: Sits opposite the start-finish over the entry to the Senna S esses, and is the only roofed grandstand on the circuit, with real seats and a clear view of the launch off the line.

Circuit Gilles Villeneuve.name: Grandstand 1 (Start-finish straight)
Circuit Gilles Villeneuve.bestFor: Start, pits, podium and ceremony — first-timers who value the ceremonial heart
pros: Grid, standing start, pit stops, finish line and podium ceremony
A giant screen sits opposite
Easy access to the main entrances and facilities
cons: You see one straight live — cornering action is on the screen
Lots of low catch-fencing obscures the corners at either end
Circuit Gilles Villeneuve.description: The main-straight stand over the pit lane, grid and podium — the ceremonial heart of the weekend, though most of the cornering action is watched on the big screen.

Circuit Gilles Villeneuve.name: Grandstand 11 (Senna S, T1–2)
Circuit Gilles Villeneuve.bestFor: Atmosphere and the start — sections 1–3 are the picks
pros: Elevated views of the start and opening corners from the higher seats
Strong lap-1 atmosphere — one of the most popular stands
Big-screen sightline
cons: Lower seats can be obstructed by the catch-fence band
Roughly 3+ km walk from the metro to this end, and no shade
Circuit Gilles Villeneuve.description: An elevated Senna Curve stand covering the start and opening corners, best from the higher seats where the view clears the fencing.

Circuit Gilles Villeneuve.name: Grandstand 12 (Senna S / climb to T3)
Circuit Gilles Villeneuve.bestFor: Best value — value-conscious fans who still want the start zone
viewsOf: Senna S (Turns 1–2), at a squarer angle
pros: Strong value — often the better-priced Senna S option (~CAD $915 3-day)
Senna S plus pit-exit action
Some seats catch the city skyline backdrop
cons: No shade
Long walk to this end of the island
Circuit Gilles Villeneuve.description: A Senna S stand with a squarer angle on the opening two corners and the climb toward Turn 3, rated the value pick of the start-zone seats with a skyline backdrop.

Circuit Gilles Villeneuve.name: Family Grandstand (T6–7 chicane)
Circuit Gilles Villeneuve.bestFor: Families with kids and spectators needing accessibility
pros: Family-friendly and accessible with a relaxed, green park setting
Adjacent to the calmer Droit du Casino GA area
cons: Low-speed corner with less raw action
Big-screen sightline needs checking
Circuit Gilles Villeneuve.description: Overlooks the Turns 6–7 chicane near the former Expo 67 Canada pavilion, with a park-and-trees atmosphere, good accessibility and family facilities.

Red Bull Ring.name: Red Bull Grandstand (sectors A–B)
Red Bull Ring.bestFor: Best overall — biggest stand, Turn 1 braking and the uphill run, festival heart of the circuit
viewsOf: uphill DRS run to Turn 3 (Remus hairpin)
pros: Largest stand on the circuit; excellent panoramic multi-corner view from mid rows up
Loudest, most party-driven atmosphere and closest to the Turn 1 Fan Zone
Three TV screens serve the stand (opposite sectors A, I/J, O/P)
cons: No cover — fully open to sun and storms
Front rows obstructed by long infield grass; A–B are premium-priced
Red Bull Ring.description: The circuit's largest stand, inside the track just past Turn 1 and running up the hill toward Turn 3, taking in Turn 1 braking, the climb to the Remus hairpin and infield Turns 6/7.

Red Bull Ring.name: T3 Grandstand
Red Bull Ring.bestFor: Best for action — head-on at the Remus hairpin (Turn 3), the #1 overtaking corner
viewsOf: the long DRS straight feeding Turn 3
pros: #1 for overtaking and incidents — lock-ups, dive-bombs and contact
Elevated and direct on the braking zone; top-tier for photography
Big screen visible
cons: No cover, and an uphill walk from the Turn 1 Fan Zone
You trade start/finish and the pits for action
Red Bull Ring.description: At the top of the circuit's steepest climb, head-on into the Remus hairpin with the long DRS straight feeding it — the best seat in the house for passes, lock-ups and contact.

Red Bull Ring.name: Steiermark Grandstand (a.k.a. Süd-West)
Red Bull Ring.bestFor: Best for first-timers — elevated, sees the start, Turn 1 chaos and the run to Turn 2/3 in one frame
pros: Sees the start and first-corner braking — pole drama and lap-1 chaos
One of the most elevated stands, with a commanding sweep of the opening sequence
Strong photography: elevation plus the long straight for head-on and panning shots
cons: Uncovered
Sells out fast, and less raw overtaking than T3
Red Bull Ring.description: Elevated outside the run into Turn 1, giving a commanding view of the main straight, the start, Turn 1 and the climb toward Turn 2/3.

Red Bull Ring.name: General Admission — Green Sector (Turns 3–4 hillside)
Red Bull Ring.bestFor: Best value — ~€160 weekend on elevated hillside sitting over the prime overtaking zone
pros: Best value on the circuit — ~€160 weekend / ~€85 race day
Elevated grass bank lifts you above much of the catch-fencing
Sits right over the prime overtaking complex
cons: Minimal shade — open hillside, exposed to sun and storms
The prime crest fills fast on race day; facilities are busier and more spread out
Red Bull Ring.description: Elevated grass hillside between Turns 3 and 4, right over the prime overtaking complex, and the best value on the circuit at roughly €160 for the weekend.

Red Bull Ring.name: Start-Ziel Grandstand (Start-Finish / Main)
Red Bull Ring.bestFor: Pit, podium and ceremony fans, plus comfort and accessibility needs
viewsOf: the start launch and finish-line crossings
pros: Covered — one of only two roofed stands
Pit stops, grid build-up, the start and the podium ceremony
Central location with the best-developed accessible facilities
cons: Less overtaking than the top of the track
Premium price for the prime A-row blocks; fencing limits low rows
Red Bull Ring.description: On the start/finish straight opposite the pits and grid — the ceremonial seat, covered, with grid build-up, pit theatre, the finish and the podium.

Red Bull Ring.name: North / Nord Grandstand
Red Bull Ring.bestFor: Comfort and shade seekers, and families wanting cover at the top of the track
pros: Covered — the standout weather-protected option at the top of the track
Commanding, elevated view of Turn 4 passing resolution
Calmer crowd than Red Bull or the GA banks
cons: About a 30–40 min walk from the main Turn 1 Fan Zone
Has sometimes been sold via restricted Dutch/Verstappen channels
Red Bull Ring.description: Covered and elevated at Turn 4 at the top of the circuit, watching passes resolve and the second DRS run.

Red Bull Ring.name: Schönberg Grandstand
Red Bull Ring.bestFor: Overtaking fans who want T3-style action from a different angle
pros: Prime DRS-zone passing and Turn 3 exit / Turn 4 entry battles
Elevated with a broad view across the upper sector
A slightly quieter alternative to T3
cons: Uncovered
Some distance to far-side action — binoculars help
Red Bull Ring.description: Beyond Turn 3 on the downhill, looking over the DRS zone and the run to Turn 4, catching the passes that start at the hairpin.

Shanghai International Circuit.name: Grandstand A Upper (Gold) — Main straight / start-finish, pits, podium
Shanghai International Circuit.bestFor: Best overall & best first-timer — the complete show (ceremony, pit theatre, screen, shade) in one seat
viewsOf: Pit lane, pit entry and pit exit
Sector 2 over the pit/paddock roof (~80% of the lap)
pros: Best all-round view at the circuit — sees ~80% of the lap over the pit roof
Fully roofed, with a large big screen and English/Mandarin audio
Closest to main entrances, toilets, food and the fan zone
cons: Priciest ticket at the circuit
Far from the back-straight overtaking; can catch a cold wind
Shanghai International Circuit.description: The elevated, fully covered Gold deck of the huge main grandstand opposite the pits, giving grid, pit stops and podium plus a view over the pit roof into Sector 2 — roughly 80% of the circuit.

Shanghai International Circuit.name: Grandstand A Platinum — Main straight (covered lounge seating)
Shanghai International Circuit.bestFor: Money-no-object comfort — climate-controlled lounge and catering with the fullest front-of-house view
pros: Covered, indoor temperature-controlled lounge with food and drink
Top pick for grid, pit and podium photography
cons: View gain over Gold is marginal — you are buying comfort, not sightline
Poor value for pure racing
Shanghai International Circuit.description: The premium covered section of Grandstand A with an indoor climate-controlled lounge and catering, rated the most comfortable seat at the circuit though its view is only marginally better than Gold.

Shanghai International Circuit.name: Grandstand B — End of main straight into Turns 1–3
pros: Crystal-clear sightlines into the opening corners and first-lap drama
Large screen faces the stand; 2–5 min walk to fan zone and facilities
cons: Completely uncovered — no shade and fully exposed to Shanghai's wet March
Lower than Grandstand A, so the far side of the track and pit complex are hidden
Shanghai International Circuit.description: Sited past the start/finish line at the Turn 1 braking point looking into the tightening T1–T3 snail, it delivers sharp first-corner action but has no roof and cannot see the rest of the lap.

Shanghai International Circuit.name: Grandstand H — End of the back straight / Turn 14 hairpin
Shanghai International Circuit.bestFor: Best value & best action — the overtaking corner, covered and cheaper than Grandstand A
viewsOf: The 1.1km back straight and slipstreaming approach
Turn 14 hairpin braking zone and apex
Final corners from the upper rows
pros: The most overtaking on the lap — divebombs, lock-ups and side-by-side exits
Partially covered with multiple screens and audio
Best action stand for photography (head-on braking and lock-up shots)
cons: About a 10 minute walk to the main amenities and fan zone
Irregular roof means cover and sightline vary seat to seat
Shanghai International Circuit.description: Positioned at the business end of the 1.1km back straight where cars brake hard for the Turn 14 hairpin, this is the prime overtaking theatre and the page's smartest spend for a racing fan.

Shanghai International Circuit.name: Grandstand K — Turn 14 hairpin exit (opposite H)
Shanghai International Circuit.bestFor: Best action (with amenities closer) — hairpin passes completed, ~5 min from food and merch
viewsOf: Second half of Turn 14 and the hairpin exit
pros: Hairpin action with a shorter amenity walk than H — closest hairpin stand to main facilities
Partially covered, with multiple screens and audio
Historically carries the accessible seating platforms
cons: Tighter sightlines than H and can feel cramped near the apex
Not the full braking-zone view — H is better for that
Shanghai International Circuit.description: Across the hairpin from H, it looks at the second half of Turn 14 and the exit, showing who completed the move and who ran wide, with facilities closer than at H.

Shanghai International Circuit.name: Grass Zone L (General Admission) — Main straight, beside Grandstand A
Shanghai International Circuit.bestFor: Best budget fallback — main-straight spectacle at GA prices, right next to the amenities
pros: Main-straight views at general-admission prices
Direct access to food, toilets and the fan zone; rarely overcrowded
cons: No seat, no shade and no big screen in-zone
GA ticket-holders are confined to their assigned zone — no roaming
Shanghai International Circuit.description: General-admission grass on the main straight next to the Main Grandstand, giving the start/finish spectacle and amenity access for budget first-timers, though there is no seat, shade or screen.

Marina Bay Street Circuit.name: Turn 2 Grandstand (Zone 1, all-zone)
Marina Bay Street Circuit.bestFor: Best overall — best all-round F1 viewer wanting the start plus first-corner action
pros: Sees the grid launch down the full start/finish straight
Best single-frame combination on the lap (T1-T2-T3)
All-zone (1-4) roaming access
cons: Uncovered
Premium price (~S$1,798 3-day)
Marina Bay Street Circuit.description: Sits perpendicular to Turn 1 looking back up the full start/finish straight and across the run-off and pit lane, and is widely rated the best seat at Marina Bay because it catches both the grid launch and the Turn 1-2-3 braking battle.

Marina Bay Street Circuit.name: Pit Grandstand (Zone 1, all-zone)
Marina Bay Street Circuit.bestFor: Best for first-timers — atmosphere, pit-stop fans, the "everything happens here" seat
pros: Grid launch, every pit stop, podium and fireworks in view
Big screens directly opposite
All-zone (1-4) roaming access
cons: Dense catch-fencing on the front straight
Premium price (~S$1,798 3-day)
Marina Bay Street Circuit.description: One of the longest grandstands in F1, running the length of the start/finish straight opposite the pit building, so it sees the grid launch, the final corner onto the straight and the whole pit lane, and it is where the podium and post-race concert fireworks happen.

Marina Bay Street Circuit.name: Turn 1 Grandstand (Zone 1, all-zone)
Marina Bay Street Circuit.bestFor: Best for action — action seekers and photographers of braking moments
pros: Highest incident probability on the lap; first-lap chaos and late-braking lunges
DRS passes arriving off the front straight
Wheelchair-accessible platform (book by phone)
cons: Uncovered
You watch the rest of the lap on screens
Marina Bay Street Circuit.description: Sits beyond the Pit stand at the first braking complex and pit exit, giving the best odds on the circuit for first-lap chaos, late-braking lunges and DRS passes off the start/finish straight.

Marina Bay Street Circuit.name: Marina Bay Grandstand (Zone 1, all-zone)
Marina Bay Street Circuit.bestFor: Photography plus race-day experience — skyline backdrop and finish-line drama
viewsOf: Final-corner exit onto the pit straight
pros: Final-corner exit and pit straight with the Marina Bay skyline behind
Superb night photography
Two big screens high on the opposite side
cons: Unreserved seating with no seat numbers — arrive early
Fencing on the straight
Marina Bay Street Circuit.description: A newer waterfront stand at the final corners (T18/19) onto the pit straight, offering the final-corner exit and the pit straight framed by the Marina Bay skyline, though seating is unreserved.

Marina Bay Street Circuit.name: Republic Grandstand (mixed zone, all-zone access)
Marina Bay Street Circuit.bestFor: Best value — value hunters who want a reserved seat plus all-zone flexibility

Reserved seating
Unusual corner-entry angle with city/skyline backdrop
cons: Not the heaviest overtaking spot
Marina Bay Street Circuit.description: Reserved seats at the Turn 4-5/6 kink near the waterfront with a skyline backdrop, and uniquely for a mid-price stand it grants Zones 1-4 access so you can still roam to the pit end and the concerts.

Marina Bay Street Circuit.name: Super Pit Grandstand (Zone 1, all-zone)

Usually includes reserved food and drink benefits
All-zone (1-4) roaming access
cons: Most expensive grandstand (~S$2,498 3-day)
Often sold out
Marina Bay Street Circuit.description: Sits above the Pit Grandstand with the same grid, pit lane and finish views from a higher vantage point, usually with reserved food and drink benefits; some vendor notes claim partial upper-deck cover but the page rates that low confidence and assumes uncovered.

Marina Bay Street Circuit.name: Padang A / Padang B Grandstands (Zone 4)
viewsOf: The near-full-throttle burst between Turns 9 and 10
pros: Cheapest seated tier (~S$738 3-day, single days from ~S$258)
Right by the Padang main concert stage
Numbered seats with backs and several big screens nearby
cons: Zone 4 only — cannot roam to the pit/start end
Not a prime overtaking corner
Marina Bay Street Circuit.description: These stands flank the short burst between Turns 9 and 10 where cars are near full throttle through a narrow section, and are picked mainly for being the cheapest seated tier and sitting right by the Padang main concert stage.

Yas Marina Circuit.name: West Grandstand (Turn 6)
Yas Marina Circuit.bestFor: Best overall & best for action — anyone who came to watch racing
pros: Widest track coverage of any stand at the circuit
DRS plus heavy braking makes it the top overtaking and incident spot
Cars brake straight toward you — excellent photography
cons: Pricier than North
No podium view and a walk/shuttle to the concert
Yas Marina Circuit.description: Sits outside Turn 6 at the end of the long back straight and wraps round so you see the braking zone, the approach straight and across the infield to Turns 15-16 — one seat, most of the lap.

Yas Marina Circuit.name: North Grandstand (Turn 5 hairpin)
Yas Marina Circuit.bestFor: Best value & best for first-timers — action, crowd and the concert walk
viewsOf: Turn 5 hairpin entry, apex and exit
The approach where cars arrive at speed
pros: Cheapest reserved seat (~AED 1,720) at a real overtaking corner
Biggest, rowdiest crowd and ~5-minute walk to the Etihad Park concert
One of the best single-corner views at the track
cons: Large runoff leaves cars a little distant
Some entry-facing seats catch late sun
Yas Marina Circuit.description: Outside the Turn 5 hairpin — sees entry, apex and exit plus the panorama back up the approach, and was the site of the 2021 title-decider.

Yas Marina Circuit.name: South Grandstand (Turn 9)
Yas Marina Circuit.bestFor: Families, comfort seekers and cornering purists
pros: High-speed cornering with visible sparks
Full roof and north-east facing, so no glare in an evening race
Sections 5-8 Level 4 give the best sightlines and screen view
cons: Fewer overtakes since the 2021 softening of the corner
Far from the concert — shuttle needed to Etihad Park
Yas Marina Circuit.description: Watches cars stream down the straight into Turn 9 and through that fast, slightly banked sweep, with upper seats also catching Turns 10-11.

Yas Marina Circuit.name: Marina Grandstand (Turns 8-9 / marina section)
viewsOf: The straight in front, between Turns 8 and 9
pros: Cheap, comfortable and the prettiest backdrop for postcard photos
Full roof, north-east facing so the sun is behind you all session
cons: Quietest stand for passing after the 2021 remodel
Section 1 rows A-D are blocked by the bridge; front blocks lose T13
Yas Marina Circuit.description: Built atop the support-pit building between Turns 8 and 9, it trades live racing action for a scenic view across the technical marina infield — sit Sections 4-5, row J and up.

Yas Marina Circuit.name: Main Grandstand (start/finish, pits & podium)
Yas Marina Circuit.bestFor: Bucket-listers who want the start, pit stops and podium ceremony
pros: The only stand with the start, pit lane and podium
Three big screens, opposite Sections 3, 6 and 8
Biggest stand with big-event buzz and the Main Oasis fan zone adjacent
cons: Most limited racing view — you watch the rest on screens
South-facing and the most sun-exposed; premium price
Yas Marina Circuit.description: Opposite the pits on the start/finish straight, it delivers lights-out, pit stops and the podium but the most limited on-track racing view at the circuit.

Yas Marina Circuit.name: Abu Dhabi Hill (General Admission)
Yas Marina Circuit.bestFor: Cheapest way in — budget and festival atmosphere over live sightlines
viewsOf: Limited track glimpses from the raised mound
pros: Cheapest ticket (~AED 995-1,250 for 3 days) with the concert included
Festival-style flexible viewing with big screens and adjacent Oasis fan zones
cons: Weak live sightlines — fencing and distance mean you watch mostly on screens
Limited shade
Yas Marina Circuit.description: The circuit's only general admission area: a raised, festival-style zone where you are buying the event and the atmosphere more than a live view of the racing.

Circuit Zandvoort.name: Main Grandstand
Circuit Zandvoort.bestFor: Best overall — cover plus grid, podium, pits and start/finish
pros: The only covered grandstand at Zandvoort
Grid, start/finish, podium ceremony and pit access
Big screen and the most accessible hard-surface facilities
cons: Most expensive (Main Straight tier)
Limited cornering action
Circuit Zandvoort.description: The biggest stand at the track and the only roofed one, giving a broad main-straight view of the grid, start/finish, podium and the DRS launch into Tarzan — the full ceremony package, weatherproofed on a coast prone to sudden rain and strong sun.

Circuit Zandvoort.name: Tarzan-In Grandstand 1 & 2 (Turn 1 / Tarzanbocht)
Circuit Zandvoort.bestFor: Best action and best value — the circuit's only real overtaking corner
pros: Highest overtaking chance on the lap, plus lap-1 chaos
Big screen and one of the best non-premium photo spots
Sensibly priced for the action — Gold-ish action for less
cons: Uncovered and fully open to the weather
Tarzan-In 3 is a trap — seated too low and loses the corner
Circuit Zandvoort.description: Sited on the outside of the wide, off-camber Turn 1 hairpin at the end of the main straight, sections 1 and 2 give an excellent view of the braking zone and apex of Zandvoort's premier overtaking corner — shoot and sit from high rows to clear the catch-fence.

Circuit Zandvoort.name: Arena Grandstands 1 & 2 (Gold, Turns 11-12)
Circuit Zandvoort.bestFor: Best for first-timers — orange-wall atmosphere, DJ and Jumbotron
pros: The best atmosphere at the circuit, with a DJ between sessions
Large triangular Jumbotron at the Turn 12 apex, visible from all Arena seats
Food, bars and merch behind the stands; Gate 2 is closest to the train
cons: Uncovered and umbrellas are banned in the stands — bring a poncho
Lower rows fight the safety fence; Arena 3 (Silver II) sightline is blocked
Circuit Zandvoort.description: A stadium bowl on the inside of Turns 11-12 with stands facing each other across the track, showing the second-best passing area — the slow chicane/hairpin braking complex — against a wall of orange, best from rows 20+ of Arena 1 (entrances 1217-1218) or Arena 2 (entrances 1209-1210).

Circuit Zandvoort.name: Arena-In Grandstand
Circuit Zandvoort.bestFor: Action seekers who want the Arena vibe a touch cheaper
pros: Hard braking into Turn 11 — overtaking-relevant
Arena atmosphere spillover
Big screen
cons: Uncovered and open to the weather
Circuit Zandvoort.description: An extension of the Arena at the Turn 11 braking zone, where late lunges and lock-ups happen, with the Arena's atmosphere spilling over.

Circuit Zandvoort.name: Arena-Out Grandstand (Arie Luyendyk, Turn 14)
Circuit Zandvoort.bestFor: Photographers chasing the signature banked-corner shot
pros: Signature banked final-corner view
Big screen
cons: Little overtaking here
Uncovered and exposed
Circuit Zandvoort.description: The last stand before the final two turns, showing cars committing to the banked Arie Luyendyk before the DRS run to Turn 1 — spectacular speed and lean rather than passing.

Circuit Zandvoort.name: Pit Grandstand
pros: Pit theatre and pit-stop sequences
Start/finish line
Big screen
cons: No cornering action of its own
Pricey (Main Straight tier)
Circuit Zandvoort.description: Sits on the main straight directly opposite the pit boxes, so you get pit-lane action, garages, the start and the launch into Tarzan — you watch cars accelerate away rather than wrestle a corner.

Circuit Zandvoort.name: Ben Pon Grandstand
Circuit Zandvoort.bestFor: Photographers fixed on the banked final corner (flagged as an avoid)
pros: Dramatic banked final-corner exit view
cons: No big screen — you lose the live race story over a 70-lap GP
No atmosphere hub nearby
Circuit Zandvoort.description: At the opposite end of the main straight from Tarzan, with a decent angle on cars firing out of the banked final corner onto the straight, but it is the one stand at Zandvoort with no big screen.
